articleTitle: Current Optimization for a Multi-Phase Machine under an Open Circuit Phase Fault Condition
publicationTitle: 2006 3rd IET International Conference on Power Electronics, Machines and Drives - PEMD 2006
abstract: In this paper, a practical method based on a symmetrical component transformation is proposed to analyze and optimize the current for a multi-phase machine under open-circuit phase conditions. Two kinds of current optimization are considered: stator copper loss minimization and inverter peak current minimization. Application of the method is described for a five-phase machine. The fault conditions investigated are single, double, and triple open-circuit phase faults. Optimized solutions for four-, six-, and seven-phase machines, with one open-circuit phase, are also presented.

articleTitle: Small-signal Stability Studies of a 270V DC More-Electric Aircraft Power System
publicationTitle: 2006 3rd IET International Conference on Power Electronics, Machines and Drives - PEMD 2006
abstract: The paper investigates the small-signal stability of a representative 270V DC power system for a more-electric aircraft, which incorporates a switched reluctance generator, under various operation conditions, including power control saturation due to current and voltage limits. Non-linear state-space models for the complete system under the various operating conditions are established, and the eigenvalue method is applied to assess the small-signal stability. Time-domain simulations are used to validate the findings of the proposed analysis technique.

articleTitle: Relationship of Modulation Schemes for Matrix Converters
publicationTitle: 2006 3rd IET International Conference on Power Electronics, Machines and Drives - PEMD 2006
abstract: This paper reveals the relationship between some well-known matrix converter modulation strategies, basic/optimum Alesina-Venturini (AV) methods and direct/indirect space vector modulation (SVM). The direct/indirect SVM methods are inherently the same. Two SVM methods are also proposed, which are equivalent to the basic/optimum AV methods respectively.

articleTitle: Mitigation of Common-mode Voltage in Matrix Converter
publicationTitle: 2006 3rd IET International Conference on Power Electronics, Machines and Drives - PEMD 2006
abstract: This paper presents a new modulation scheme for matrix converters. With the proposed method, the peak common mode voltage is reduced to 1/√3 of the input phase voltage amplitude; at least ⅔ reduction in the high order harmonics and ⅓ in RMS value are realised. Indirect space vector modulation is adopted and modified. Four active voltage vectors in the three-dimensional space are utilised to generate the desired output voltage, with reduced common mode voltage. The switching period is full filled and no zero states are implemented. Comparisons of different modulation techniques are made. Simulation results are provided to demonstrate the superior performance of the proposed scheme over conventional modulation techniques.

articleTitle: Machine and Converter Reliabilities in Wind Turbines
publicationTitle: 2006 3rd IET International Conference on Power Electronics, Machines and Drives - PEMD 2006
abstract: Electrical Machine/Converter combinations are used in a variety of applications, from powers of Watts to MegaWatts. Some applications, such as propulsion and generation, have high reliability & availability requirements. Modem large wind turbines incorporate variable pitch blades and a variable speed Generator, which feeds the Grid through a Converter and have a need for high reliability & availability. There are a number of configurations of generator and converter intended to provide optimum performance for present and future wind power. This paper describes an investigation into the reliabilities of Generators and Converters in such configurations and is based on failure data collected in Germany and Denmark. The paper draws conclusions about which configurations have the higher reliability and identifies the subassemblies of the turbines which require attention for the future design of high reliability wind turbines. Recommendations are made about how designers and operators of wind turbines can increase their reliability by the choice of Concept and the operating regime

articleTitle: Grid Power Quality Improvements Using Grid-Coupled Hybrid Electric Vehicles PEMD 2006
publicationTitle: 2006 3rd IET International Conference on Power Electronics, Machines and Drives - PEMD 2006
abstract: The paper examines the interaction between grid-coupled full hybrid electric vehicles (HEV) and the grid. The interaction allows the hybrid vehicle to travel a significant part of the time in all-electric mode. On the other hand, the grid coupling allows the grid to use the hybrid car as a controllable load and energy storage facility, enabling a higher penetration of variable generation units, such as renewable sources based on wind and photovoltaic cells. Experiments with a battery, grid connection and induction machine prove the feasibility of these grid-coupled hybrid electric vehicles.

articleTitle: Linked Electromagnetic and Thermal Modelling of a Permanent Magnet Motor
publicationTitle: 2006 3rd IET International Conference on Power Electronics, Machines and Drives - PEMD 2006
abstract: This paper studies the thermal modelling of a permanent magnet motor using linked commercial design packages. The electromagnetic design is carried out using SPEED PC-BDC, from The University of Glasgow while the thermal simulation, to verify the thermal integrity of the machine, is carried out using Motor-CAD, from Motor Design Ltd. These two design procedures are often carried out separately but this illustrates that, in the modem Windows environment, it is often possible to link packages together and bring a stepchange to the sophistication of the design procedure. The results are verified experimentally.

articleTitle: On-line Monitoring of the MOSFET Device Junction Temperature by Computation of the Threshold Voltage
publicationTitle: 2006 3rd IET International Conference on Power Electronics, Machines and Drives - PEMD 2006
abstract: A method for an on-line junction temperature measurement is introduced. The circuit allows the calibration of a real-time thermal model of a power MOSFET. A regular calibration of the real-time model provides an accurate thermal flux model over the lifetime of the power MOSFET. The measurement of threshold voltage is used to determine the device temperature. The paper presents the on-line measurement method, the circuit and test results.

articleTitle: Determination of Thermal Cross-Coupling Effects in Multi-Device Power Electronic Modules
publicationTitle: 2006 3rd IET International Conference on Power Electronics, Machines and Drives - PEMD 2006
abstract: A dynamic thermal model is developed for a 350A half bridge IGBT module and cooler which includes the effects of thermal cross-coupling between the various semiconductor elements. The parameters for the model are extracted from measurements of the transient thermal impedance from junction to ambient. A matrix representation of the model is developed which in turn is implemented into a working model in PSpice by use of a multi-term R-C network. Simulation results show that the cross-coupling effects during load power cycling are not negligible and are dependent on the load power frequency. It is concluded that typical thermal models derived from manufacturers' data may significantly underestimate junction temperature elevation in multi-device power modules.

articleTitle: Design of a Five-Phase Induction Motor using Flux Distribution Optimisation
publicationTitle: 2006 3rd IET International Conference on Power Electronics, Machines and Drives - PEMD 2006
abstract: The design of a five-phase induction motor stator by finite element analysis is discussed. Stator slot dimensioning to ensure optimised flux distribution with respect to five-phase winding systems is presented. The motor is constructed and tested to demonstrate conformance of the practical motor with the FEA model.

articleTitle: PEBB - Power Electronics Building Blocks, from Concept to Reality
publicationTitle: 2006 3rd IET International Conference on Power Electronics, Machines and Drives - PEMD 2006
abstract: The Power Electronics Building Block (PEBB) concept is a platform-based approach where basic building blocks are consistent with one another, have a defined functionality, standardized hardware & control interfaces. Adoption of building blocks for multiple applications, results in high volume production, and reductions in engineering effort, design testing, onsite installation and maintenance work. U.S. Navy's Office of Naval Research (ONR) has funded several universities and manufacturers to apply the PEBB concept to a broad range of applications. This paper describes the evolution of PEBB from concept to reality in already delivered products.

articleTitle: Modal Analysis of a Grid Connected Doubly-Fed Induction Generator
publicationTitle: 2006 3rd IET International Conference on Power Electronics, Machines and Drives - PEMD 2006
abstract: This paper presents the modal analysis of a grid connected doubly-fed induction generator. The inherent oscillating modes of the DFIG are determined with the single machine infinite bus power system model. The effects of initial rotor speed and grid strength on the machine dynamics are studied. The conditions for which stator transients can be neglected are also determined. articleTitle: Simple Almost Zero Switching Losses for Interleaved Boost Converter
publicationTitle: 2006 3rd IET International Conference on Power Electronics, Machines and Drives - PEMD 2006
abstract: Control and applications of DC/DC converter has been widely discussed in power electronics and control literature. Soft-switching strategies are used instead of hard switching to avoid or minimize commutation losses; however soft switching topologies use a resonant or some form of partial resonant commutation with prohibited high circulating energy in medium and high power applications. In this work, a simple converter configuration to achieve almost zero switching losses is proposed for the interleaved boost converter. Simulation, practical implementing issues and limitations of the proposed scheme during different test conditions are shown.

articleTitle: A Wavelet Controller for Shunt Active Power Filter
publicationTitle: 2006 3rd IET International Conference on Power Electronics, Machines and Drives - PEMD 2006
abstract: A wavelet-based controller for shunt active power filter (APF) has been proposed in this paper. The constructed controller based on multi resolution analysis has the advantage of better frequency bandwidth selection. The tuning parameters of the controllers are the gains to be applied to the time-frequency signals at different resolutions. This has the advantage of aiding the process of a proper choice of coefficients of tuning parameters. The developed simulation model of the APF with wavelet-based control shows satisfactory steady state and dynamic performance. A comparison with standard PI controller shows that the dynamic response of the proposed wavelet controller is much faster. This is of advantage in specific applications where the fast dynamic response of the controller is of importance to achieve a desired reference within a short duration of time. The novel technique of the generation of control signal ensures that even when the steady state error is zero, the controller can generate a steady control signal. The wavelet data window width is chosen optimally such that frequencies above 600 Hz are eliminated. This avoids the generation of high frequency spikes in the reference control current signal and ensures stability.

articleTitle: Predicting and Preventing Demagnetisation in Permanent Magnet Motor Drives
publicationTitle: 2006 3rd IET International Conference on Power Electronics, Machines and Drives - PEMD 2006
abstract: This paper presents a case study. An existing PMSM design was moved to a new application with higher operating temperatures and higher peak currents. Substantial rotor demagnetisation was observed in the new application where no problem had been observed previously. The causes of the demagnetisation are presented, along with analysis of the magnetic circuit. The analysis is correlated with experimental results. The effects of machine design are considered. A solution to the problem is proposed and tested and again the analysis is correlated with the results. Finally some guidelines are proposed for the design of robust PM machines and the associated drive electronics.

articleTitle: Modelling of Magnetic Field Pollution Generated by Power Transformers
publicationTitle: 2006 3rd IET International Conference on Power Electronics, Machines and Drives - PEMD 2006
abstract: In this paper the modelling of stray magnetic field produced by power transformer is presented. Two different numerical codes based on 3D Finite Integration Technique of the electromagnetic field have been adopted and the results are compared with experimental ones. The main purpose of the presented investigation is to improve the knowledge about modelling of power transformers in order to better estimate the low frequency magnetic field pollution produced by substation power transformers.

articleTitle: A Study of Inverter Loss Reduction Using Discontinuous Pulse Width Modulation Techniques
publicationTitle: 2006 3rd IET International Conference on Power Electronics, Machines and Drives - PEMD 2006
abstract: In this paper, the reduction in inverter losses by using various forms of Discontinuous Pulse Width Modulation (DPWM) scheme is investigated. Models for various forms of DPWM excitation have been implemented using Pspice and these have been combined with an existing model for a three-phase voltage source inverter. The models were then used to predict inverter losses and these have been verified by direct measurements in a calorimeter. Both simulated and measured results confirm the expectation that DPWM can reduce losses, and that optimum variant depends on load conditions. Reductions in losses in the range 5 to 10% can be expected by appropriate choice of variant. Measurements of inverter losses have been made for an induction motor load operating under a range of conditions and these again show how the optimum choice of scheme depends on load conditions.

articleTitle: A Novel High-Speed Flux Reversal Alternator
publicationTitle: 2006 3rd IET International Conference on Power Electronics, Machines and Drives - PEMD 2006
abstract: This paper introduces a novel two-phase flux reversal permanent magnet alternator for high-speed applications. The altemator has four magnets, four-pole stators and two-pole rotor and is categorized as a doubly salient permanent magnet machine (DSPM). Due to a low number of poles, this structure is suitable for high-speed applications, so that frequency is minimized and iron losses decreased. Also, a double-stator structure is used to compensate energy in each cycle. The principle of operation, design, modelling and finite element analysis of the alternator are investigated in this paper.

articleTitle: Cage Motor Faults Detection by Speed Estimation and Spectral Current Analysis
publicationTitle: 2006 3rd IET International Conference on Power Electronics, Machines and Drives - PEMD 2006
abstract: A proposed algorithm for the detection and localization of rotor faults in a squirrel cage induction machine is presented in this paper. This algorithm uses the behavior of the current spectral analysis and the estimation of the rotor speed to detect bars faults in three phase induction machine. In order to simulate the faulty motor behavior, a mathematical model is being adopted and simulation results obtained verifies well the performance of the proposed algorithm.

articleTitle: Optimisation of BDFM Stator Design Using an Equivalent Circuit Model and a Search Method
publicationTitle: 2006 3rd IET International Conference on Power Electronics, Machines and Drives - PEMD 2006
abstract: This paper presents an iterative method for the stator design optimisation of the Brushless Doubly-Fed Machine (BDFM) based on a per phase equivalent circuit model and a tabu search method. Maximum power output from a frame size 180 BDFM is obtained by optimally dividing the overall electric and magnetic loadings between the stator windings. Parameters of the per phase equivalent circuit are calculated according to geometric dimensions for different designs. The relationship between BDFM power output and the control winding excitation is discussed. Comparisons between the original and optimised stator designs are given with experimental verifications.

articleTitle: Averaged Modelling, Simulation and Linear Control Design of a PWM Fixed Frequency Three-Phase Four-Wire Shunt Active Power Filter for a Typical Industrial Load
publicationTitle: 2006 3rd IET International Conference on Power Electronics, Machines and Drives - PEMD 2006
abstract: Current harmonics, which are injected in the utility by nonlinear loads, cause major problems that tend to deteriorate the power quality at the mains. To reduce such harmonics, Active Power Filters (APF) are commonly employed. In this paper, a new constant-frequency control scheme for a shunt three-phase four-wire APF is proposed. The APF is used to compensate the current distortion and the reactive power created by a typical industrial load. The elaboration of the control law is based on a small-signal averaged model of the converter, computed in the (d,q,O) synchronous frame. The control scheme consists of multiple-loops PI controllers that ensure voltage regulation at the DC side of the filter, and current wave shaping at the AC side. The control system is implemented numerically using Matlab/Simulink tool. The performance of the proposed control approach is finally discussed through the obtained simulation results.

articleTitle: Designs of Claw-Pole Motors for Industrial Applications
publicationTitle: 2006 3rd IET International Conference on Power Electronics, Machines and Drives - PEMD 2006
abstract: Recently, it has been shown that a special claw pole motor construction could give a torque density of 1.5 Nm/kg at a power factor of 0.87 for a servo motor application [8]. The previous investigation was restricted to motors having a maximum outer diameter of 115 mm in order to utilise available materials. This paper addresses the question whether or not such a special type of claw-pole motor, with claws both in the rotor and in the stator, can compete with conventional motors with respect to torque density, power factor, efficiency and cost, allowing the size and construction (like intemal or external rotor) to vary. Results identifying what are considered the best applications for the claw-pole motors and for what power output is presented.

articleTitle: Modifying the Inertial Response of Power-Converter Based Wind Turbine Generators
publicationTitle: 2006 3rd IET International Conference on Power Electronics, Machines and Drives - PEMD 2006
abstract: Inertial response is an important phenomena exhibited by conventional power system connected generators. Inertial response plays an extremely important role in achieving the constant supply-demand energy balance. For conventional generators, inertial response is an inherent characteristic due to the coupling of their rotational speed to the power system frequency. Modem power generation systems such as variable speed wind turbines utilise power converters to decouple the turbines rotational speed from the system frequency. This variable speed operation offers advantages both in increased energy capture and smoother power production. A disadvantage of power-converter based variable speed operation is that it usually results in the loss of the important inertial response. The loss of inertial response can be prevented through the addition of a supplementary control loop in power converter based wind turbines.

articleTitle: Eddy-Current Losses in the Solid Back-Iron of Permanent-Magnet Machines with Concentrated Fractional Pitch Windings
publicationTitle: 2006 3rd IET International Conference on Power Electronics, Machines and Drives - PEMD 2006
abstract: The objective of this paper is to calculate the eddy-current losses in the solid back-iron of permanent-magnet (PM) machines with concentrated fractional-pitch stator windings. PM machines with fractional-pitch stator windings are increasingly used a lot because of their cost-effectiveness. The paper derives a model for these eddy-current losses. Although the correlation between the model and the measurements is not perfect, some important conclusions can be drawn. In machines with full-pitch distributed windings, the eddy-current losses in the back-iron are negligible, while in machines with fractional-pitch windings, these losses are too high to be acceptable.

articleTitle: Inverter-based microgrids: Small-signal modelling and testing
publicationTitle: 2006 3rd IET International Conference on Power Electronics, Machines and Drives - PEMD 2006
abstract: In this paper, a systematic way of developing a small-signal state-space model of the inverter-based microgrids is presented. Each sub-module is modeled in state-space form and all are combined together on a common reference frame. The complete model is linearized around an operating point and the resulting system matrix is used to derive the eigenvalues. The eigenvalues (termed 'modes') indicate the frequency and damping of oscillatory components in the transient response. A sensitivity analysis is also presented which helps identifying the origin of each of the modes and identify possible feedback signals for design of controllers to improve the system stability. Results from the model are verified against a prototype microgrid experimental setup.

articleTitle: A Novel Cost Effective Edge-Resonant Soft-Switching PWM High Frequency Inverter with Reduced Circuit Component
publicationTitle: 2006 3rd IET International Conference on Power Electronics, Machines and Drives - PEMD 2006
abstract: This paper presents a cost effective edge-resonant soft-switching PWM high frequency inverter with minimum circuit components. This inverter can achieve wider soft commutation, simpler circuit configuration, smaller volumetric size, lower cost and wider power regulation range, higher-efficiency as compared to single ended quasi-resonant ZVS-PFM and active voltage clamped quasi-resonant ZVS-PWM inverters. The practical effectiveness of a novel type edge-resonant soft-switching PWM high frequency inverter using IGBT is actually proved for consumer induction heated appliances. Experimental and simulation results are agreed reasonably.

articleTitle: Effect of Supply-Voltage Unbalance on Voltage-Source Inverter
publicationTitle: 2006 3rd IET International Conference on Power Electronics, Machines and Drives - PEMD 2006
abstract: Properties of the control method for the compensation of unbalanced voltage supply that eliminates pulsating current in the DC bus of a voltage source inverter are analyzed. These pulsations can have negative effects on operating properties of the drive as well as on the quality of power supply in the electrical vicinity of the inverter. The impact of the control method on the power factors and current amplitudes in individual input phases as well as current unbalance and total power factor for the available range of control parameters is analyzed.

articleTitle: On the Calculation of Harmonic Air-Gap Fields in Machines with Single-Sided Slotting
publicationTitle: 2006 3rd IET International Conference on Power Electronics, Machines and Drives - PEMD 2006
abstract: In this paper the authors develop a method that enables the interaction of stator mmf and air-gap permeance harmonics to be systematically accounted for by harmonic correction factors. The work is verified by means of measurements made on a specially-constructed test rig.

articleTitle: Investigation of Microgrids
publicationTitle: 2006 3rd IET International Conference on Power Electronics, Machines and Drives - PEMD 2006
abstract: A three phase Microgrid test rig with representative power loads, rotating generation and an energy storage system has been designed and built. This paper describes the test rig and the use of the test rig in developing the energy storage interface control.

articleTitle: A Voltage-Fed Series Load Resonant High Frequency Inverter with ZCS-PDM Scheme for Induction-Heated Fusing Roller and Extended Circuit Topologies
publicationTitle: 2006 3rd IET International Conference on Power Electronics, Machines and Drives - PEMD 2006
abstract: This paper presents the two lossless auxiliary inductors-assisted voltage source type half bridge (single ended push pull: SEPP) series resonant high frequency inverter for induction heated fusing roller in copy and printing machines. The simple high-frequency inverter treated here can completely achieve stable zero current soft switching (ZCS) commutation for wide its output power regulation ranges and load variations under constant high frequency pulse density modulation (PDM) scheme. Its transient and steady state operating principle is originally described and discussed for a constant high-frequency PDM control strategy under a stable ZCS operation commutation, together with its output effective power regulation characteristics-based on the high frequency PDM strategy. The experimental operating performances of this voltage source SEPP ZCS-PDM series resonant high frequency inverter using IGBTs are illustrated as compared with computer simulation results and experimental ones. Its power losses analysis and actual efficiency are evaluated and discussed on the basis of simulation and experimental results. The feasible effectiveness of this high frequency inverter appliance implemented here is proved from the practical point of view.

Author Keywords: Voltage source types series load resonant inverter
Induction heated roller in copy and printing machines

articleTitle: Development of a Portable Braille Display Using a Fast Prototyping Platform for Power Electronics
publicationTitle: 2006 3rd IET International Conference on Power Electronics, Machines and Drives - PEMD 2006
abstract: This paper presents the design of a horizontal rotating wheel Braille display, using the advantages of a fast prototyping platform for power electronics (FPP). The prototyping platform performs the control of four linear electromagnetic actuators, one DC-motor and can communicate via a serial link with a PC.

articleTitle: Solid Rotor Induction Machines for use in Electrically-Assisted Turbochargers
publicationTitle: 2006 3rd IET International Conference on Power Electronics, Machines and Drives - PEMD 2006
abstract: The stator leakage reactance has a major influence on the performance of a solid rotor induction machine. It is larger and it is more difficult to define and calculate than in a cagerotor machine. When the higher leakage reactance is taken into account, the equivalent circuit model gives predictions of sufficient precision for design purposes. The airgap, normally chosen to be quite small, is preferably quite large by general standards. The torque varies as (V/f)3 which makes it difficult to provide a wide range of constant power operation in a variable speed application. Slitting the rotor helps to improve the characteristic for variable-speed duties.

articleTitle: Design and Construction of a Magnetic Fault Current Limiter
publicationTitle: 2006 3rd IET International Conference on Power Electronics, Machines and Drives - PEMD 2006
abstract: A fault current limiter using permanent magnets has been designed and its performance simulated using a two-dimensional dimensional time-stepping finite-element method incorporating a model of hysteresis for hard magnetic materials.

articleTitle: Comparison of Stray Load and Inverter-Induced Harmonic Losses in Induction Motors Using Calorimetric and Harmonic Injection Methods
publicationTitle: 2006 3rd IET International Conference on Power Electronics, Machines and Drives - PEMD 2006
abstract: This paper addresses two types of additional losses in induction motors. One is stray load loss resulting from loss segregation when induction motors operate from a sinusoidal supply voltage and the other is harmonic loss when induction motors operate from inverter-fed supply voltage. Both losses are of concern in machine design and operation but they are difficult to predict accurately without the use of empirical factors. This is due to their complex loss mechanisms and small magnitudes in most cases. Investigation into the correlation of the two loss components could enable effective quality control of the manufacturing of machines for use on inverter supplies. With the availability of advanced calorimetric and harmonic injection techniques, it becomes possible for these small loss components to be measured with precision. In this paper, seven induction motors ranging in power through 1.1, 7.5, 15 to 30 kW are tested for experimental comparison. Among these are four 7.5 kW machines. Test results suggest there is a need for induction motors designed specifically for inverter-fed operation.

articleTitle: Interior Permanent-Magnet Synchronous Machine Design by Reluctants Networks Approach for Hybrid Vehicle Applications
publicationTitle: 2006 3rd IET International Conference on Power Electronics, Machines and Drives - PEMD 2006
abstract: Finite Element Method (FEM) design yields results exhibiting a high level of accuracy, yet remains a time-consuming procedure. In this paper, an analytical model for the interior permanent-magnet synchronous machine's (IPMSM) design state is presented. A methodological design, composed of four principal steps, will also be shown. A comparison with FEM allows validating the proposed methodology, which enables quickly determining several machines capable of satisfying a given set of specifications.

articleTitle: Deadbeat Controller for Bidirectional High-Frequency Link Inverter
publicationTitle: 2006 3rd IET International Conference on Power Electronics, Machines and Drives - PEMD 2006
abstract: This paper presents a Deadbeat controller for Bidirectional High-Frequency Link (BHFL) inverter. The proposed controller consists of inner current loop, outer voltage loop and a feedforward controller. Additional disturbance decoupling networks are employed to improve the robustness of the system towards load variations. This takes into account the model discretisation effect. Therefore, accurate disturbance decoupling can be achieved. A lkVA prototype inverter is constructed and the performances of the proposed controller are experimentally verified. The results show that the proposed controller has very fast dynamic response, and good steady-state response even under highly nonlinear loads.

articleTitle: Airgap Eccentricity Fault Diagnosis, in Three-Phase Induction Motors, by the Instantaneous Power Signature Analysis
publicationTitle: 2006 3rd IET International Conference on Power Electronics, Machines and Drives - PEMD 2006
abstract: This paper firstly presents a modelling and simulation study concerning the occurrence of airgap eccentricity in three-phase induction motors. For that purpose, the Winding Function Approach was considered. Then, the instantaneous power spectrum is used as a tool for the detection of mixed airgap eccentricity condition in operating three-phase squirrel cage induction motors. Both simulation and experimental results are presented to show that the amount of information carried by the instantaneous power spectrum is higher than the one extracted from the motor current signature analysis, which illustrates the merits of the proposed approach.

articleTitle: Improving the Starting Torque in External-Rotor Induction Motors Using an Outer Can
publicationTitle: 2006 3rd IET International Conference on Power Electronics, Machines and Drives - PEMD 2006
abstract: The paper presents a model for an external-rotor squirrel-cage induction motor, where the cage rings are short-circuited (shunted) by a conducting outer can joining the two rings. It is found that this improves the cooling and operating characteristics. This end-ring shunting effect is discussed and new equivalent circuits for the rotor established. The special features of this machine are determined by consideration of the magnetic field. Tests and results are presented to highlight the operation of this induction motor configuration.

articleTitle: A New High Efficiency Line Start Motor with High Starting Torque
publicationTitle: 2006 3rd IET International Conference on Power Electronics, Machines and Drives - PEMD 2006
abstract: A new electrical machine which starts directly on line and does not require power electronics has been developed. Compared with the standard line start induction motor it has about 30% less losses and a similar starting performance. The new machine has a conventional stator and a two part rotor.

articleTitle: An Integrated Machine and Matrix Converter based High Power Rudder EMA
publicationTitle: 2006 3rd IET International Conference on Power Electronics, Machines and Drives - PEMD 2006
abstract: This paper describes the design, construction and testing of an integrated Electro-Mechanical Actuator (EMA) using a Permanent Magnet Motor drive by a Matrix Converter. The design of the integrated system has included the motor, the power converter and the thermal integration with the EMA. Practical results from the converter are presented for a range of test conditions.

articleTitle: Evaluation of the Planar and Normal Forces of an Electromagnetic Planar Actuator
publicationTitle: 2006 3rd IET International Conference on Power Electronics, Machines and Drives - PEMD 2006
abstract: This paper describes an analytical method to compute the static planar and normal forces of an electromagnetic planar actuator. The actuator has a mover with two permanent magnets. Its movement can take place along the x-axis and yaxis simultaneously, according to the direction of the propulsion planar force produced. A normal force is also present as an attraction force between the mover and the armature core. The planar force is computed by means of Lorentz force. The normal force was obtained by means of Maxwell Stress Tensor. The analytical models were validated by means of a Finite Element model and by experimental results.

articleTitle: A Predictive Current Control Scheme for a Hybrid AC/AC Direct Power Converter
publicationTitle: 2006 3rd IET International Conference on Power Electronics, Machines and Drives - PEMD 2006
abstract: The Hybrid ac/ac Direct Power Converter (HDPC) has the advantage of improved voltage transfer ratio and higher robustness against supply voltage unbalances over the Conventional Matrix Converters (CMC). The HDPC also has the inherent advantages of the CMC such as: adjustable input power factor, sinusoidal supply currents and no bulky energy storage elements which reduce the life time of the converter. This paper proposed a predictive current controller scheme for a HDPC based on 2-stage matrix converter providing unity voltage transfer ratios; even in the case the supply voltage is highly unbalanced. The proposed predictive current controller is simple in digital implementation, provides higher bandwidth control, requires no additional circuitry and maintains a constant switching frequency which allows synchronizing the switching of the HDPC for sinusoidal supply currents.

articleTitle: Stability Analysis for Aircraft On-Board System
publicationTitle: 2006 3rd IET International Conference on Power Electronics, Machines and Drives - PEMD 2006
abstract: Vehicles of the future will store, transport and use large amounts of electrical energy. The main components of DC networks are power electronic converters. Combinations of such converters are known to be unstable in certain situations. By investigating the causes of instability and comparing current methods, a state space representation is chosen for converter modelling. The concepts of sensitivity and participation factors applied to network models are proposed to address the requirement for algorithms aimed at optimisation. Conclusions are drawn for converters under development for aircraft systems. Thanks to this method, passive elements are optimised by reducing their global weight and volume.

articleTitle: An Interface for Renewable Energy Sources using a Multilevel Rectifier with Enhanced DC Link Control
publicationTitle: 2006 3rd IET International Conference on Power Electronics, Machines and Drives - PEMD 2006
abstract: This paper the control of the neutral point current in a Neutral Point Clamped Rectifier. This control ensures that the voltages across the DC link capacitors remain equal, even in the presence of unbalanced loads or sources in the DC side. The method employs an offset which is added to each of the inverter modulation waves. This offset causes a zero sequence voltage in the rectifier which can drive the desired neutral point current to counteract the unbalanced capacitor currents. Simulation and experimental results confirm the method.

articleTitle: Implementation and Verification of CFL Models for Use in Performance Analysis in High Frequency Electronic Ballasts
publicationTitle: 2006 3rd IET International Conference on Power Electronics, Machines and Drives - PEMD 2006
abstract: The performance of a 42 W compact fluorescent lamp and its associated electronic ballast has been simulated in PSPICE. Both behavioural and physics-based models for the lamp were considered and the former was found to give good results with the benefit of easy implementation. The predictions of circuit currents and losses closely match experimentally measured values. Losses were measured directly in a calorimeter. Using simulation to disaggregate the total loss figure, it is seen that the output resonant inductor makes the largest contribution to the total losses in the electronic ballast.

articleTitle: Design and Optimisation of Two phase Tubular Permanent Magnet Linear Motors for Custom Applications
publicationTitle: 2006 3rd IET International Conference on Power Electronics, Machines and Drives - PEMD 2006
abstract: Tubular Permanent Magnet Linear Motor are involved in a lot of industrial application as alternative to pneumatic linear actuators. The design of these devices requires to take into account several constraints and specification. The use of finite element analysis allows to estimate several phenomena like end effects, force ripple and non linearity. At the same time the calculation time required is very large. For this reason the optimization procedure proposed is based on genetic algorithms (GA) coupled with Generalized Response Surface method which interpolates the objective function of the problem. In this way the calculation time is reduced and a good exploration of objective function is possible.

articleTitle: Evaluation of stator iron loss in tubular permanent magnet machines by three-dimensional finite element analysis
publicationTitle: 2006 3rd IET International Conference on Power Electronics, Machines and Drives - PEMD 2006
abstract: This paper evaluates the stator iron loss in a tubular permanent magnet (PM) machine equipped with a laminated stator core by three-dimensional (3-D) finite element (FE) analysis, and quantifies the influence of the laminated modules on the iron loss. The 3-D FE model accounts for the non-linear, anisotropic magnetisation characteristic of the laminated stator structure, and for the voids which exist between the laminated modules. Predicted results are compared with those deduced from an axi-symmetric (2-D) FE model which cannot account for the influence of the voids. It is shown that the no-load iron loss which is calculated from the 3-D FE model is virtually the same as that which is deduced from the 2-D FE model. However, on full-load the iron loss which is determined from the 3-D model is significantly lower than that which is predicted from the 2-D model, primarily as a consequence of the teeth and yoke being more highly saturated, due to the presence of the voids in the laminated stator core. However, if the width of the tooth and yoke sections of the I-shaped laminations from which the laminated modules are fabricated is increased to achieve the same effective tooth and yoke areas as in the 2-D model, the difference in the iron loss predicted from the 2-D and 3-D FE models becomes insignificant.

articleTitle: A Novel Switched Reluctance Generator Inverter Topology for AC Power Generation
publicationTitle: 2006 3rd IET International Conference on Power Electronics, Machines and Drives - PEMD 2006
abstract: The paper investigates the operation of a novel sparse power converter for the switched reluctance generator for generating ac power. This will eliminate requirement of two stages of power conversion generating into power supply. The performance of the converter is investigated and simulation results are presented.

articleTitle: Chaos Phenomena in Cascaded Buck Converter
publicationTitle: 2006 3rd IET International Conference on Power Electronics, Machines and Drives - PEMD 2006
abstract: A study has been done for chaos and bifurcation phenomena in a current controlled two stage buck converter. It is found that the converter moves from periodic operation to chaotic operation as the input voltage to the converter is reduced. The bifurcation pathway includes smooth period-doubling bifurcations as well as border collision bifurcations. This knowledge is vital for designing practical circuits in power electronics.

articleTitle: Application of Wavelet Transformation for the Identification of High Frequency Spurious Signals in Step Down DC - DC Converter Circuits Experiencing Intermittent Chaotic Patterns
publicationTitle: 2006 3rd IET International Conference on Power Electronics, Machines and Drives - PEMD 2006
abstract: Intermittent chaotic phenomena can appear in a dc-dc step down converter when the later is coupled with spurious high frequency signals. It is therefore important to understand why and how these phenomena occur and what is their relationship with the frequency characterises of the spurious injected signals. This paper uses a fast wavelet transform to isolate the frequency of these signals even when the converter is in a chaotic or subharmonic mode of operation.

articleTitle: Technology Comparison for Cascaded Multilevel Converters in Distribution Networks
publicationTitle: 2006 3rd IET International Conference on Power Electronics, Machines and Drives - PEMD 2006
abstract: This paper compares technology for two structures of cascaded multilevel converter for 11kV and 33kV distribution networks on the basis of power losses in IGBT. First, is traditional cascaded converter which has equal-sized cells in its chain and the other is the recently proposed chain with a ternary relationship between its dc-link voltages. Models with 81 and 27 levels are developed for both kinds of converter after selection of suitable IGBT device technology for comparative analysis. The total power losses in IGBTs and diode of each cell in the chain are estimated by simulation and it has been concluded that conduction losses are dominant everywhere. The equal-sized converter is only useful with 27-levels in 33kV system whereas the ternary-sequence converter produces lower losses in the other cases and especially so for the 81-level converter in the 11kV network.

articleTitle: Some Design Aspects Concerning a New Three-Phase AC/DC PWM Converter for Four Quadrant Performance
publicationTitle: 2006 3rd IET International Conference on Power Electronics, Machines and Drives - PEMD 2006
abstract: A new and original ac/dc three-phase converter suitable to be applied in DC catenary's power systems for electric traction is presented. The overall control strategy for providing constant DC voltage, Pulse-Width Modulation (PWM) signal generation, and simulation results are also presented. The proposed converter topology uses twelve power switches (three legs) and an inductor-capacitor dc-bus. This converter is able to simulate infinite DC busbar performance, providing constant, load independent, output voltage, giving the advantages of a good Power Factor (PF), a low Total Harmonic Distortion (THD), and smaller filters.

articleTitle: Losses of a Permanent Magnet Synchronous Motor with Concentrated Windings
publicationTitle: 2006 3rd IET International Conference on Power Electronics, Machines and Drives - PEMD 2006
abstract: This paper deals with loss calculations of low speed 45 kW permanent magnet synchronous motors with concentrated windings. All motors calculated have the same frame size, air-gap diameter, air-gap length and the same amount of permanent magnet material. Finite element method (Cedrat Flux2D) and analytical method are used in calculations. Losses calculated with both methods are compared and losses of motors with different pole pair numbers are compared as well.

articleTitle: Modelling and GB Grid Code Compliance Studies of Offshore Wind Farms with Doubly-Fed Induction Generators
publicationTitle: 2006 3rd IET International Conference on Power Electronics, Machines and Drives - PEMD 2006
abstract: The number and total capacity of large offshore wind farms connected to the GB power supply network is going to increase considerably in the next years. The Doubly-Fed Induction Generator seems to be the preferable technology for offshore wind farms at the moment, at least in the UK. Average time-invariant models are usually used for the representation of Doubly-Fed Induction Generators. The validity of the approach is investigated by comparing the steady state and dynamic behaviour of such a model with a time variant model of the frequency converter of the DFIG, where the power electronic switches are represented. The commercial software PSCAD/EMTDC is used. Consequently, the compliance of an offshore wind farm with DFIGs with the GB Grid Code is examined in respect to the strength of the power supply network at the PoC and the electrical distance to the PoC. Nomenclature DFIG PoC SCL VSI Doubly-Fed Induction Generator Point of Connection Short Circuit Level Voltage Source Inverter

articleTitle: Condition Monitoring of an Induction Machine using a Stochastic Search Technique
publicationTitle: 2006 3rd IET International Conference on Power Electronics, Machines and Drives - PEMD 2006
abstract: This paper describes the principles of a new technique for electrical condition monitoring of the stator and rotor circuits in an induction machine. Using time-domain terminal voltages and currents with rotor position data, a stochastic search technique (simulated annealing) is able to confirm that the machine windings are healthy, or indicate that there is a fault and provide information about the location and nature of the fault. The technique is demonstrated using experimental data from a laboratory machine with both armature and secondary winding faults.

articleTitle: Super Capacitor based Energy Storage as Peak Power Unit in the Applications of Hybrid Electric Vehicles
publicationTitle: 2006 3rd IET International Conference on Power Electronics, Machines and Drives - PEMD 2006
abstract: Fuel cells and batteries are expected to gradually replace combustion engines as the main power supply systems of hybrid electric vehicles. With super capacitor based energy storage presented in this paper, they are ensured to operate in the good operation conditions without reducing the dynamics on the drive train. Thus high efficiency and good lifecycle can be achieved.

articleTitle: Transient Performance Evaluation of a Five-Phase Series-Connected Two-Motor Drive
publicationTitle: 2006 3rd IET International Conference on Power Electronics, Machines and Drives - PEMD 2006
abstract: The paper reports the results of an experimental investigation of a multi-phase two-motor drive system, consisting of a series connection of a five-phase induction machine (IM) and a five-phase synchronous reluctance machine (Syn-Rel). The two machines are controlled independently although a single five-phase voltage source inverter is used as the supply. A brief overview of the operating principles is provided first. This is followed by a description of the experimental rig. Decoupling of control within the two-motor drive is illustrated by means of experimental results, which visualise the dynamic performance of the vector-controlled drive system during acceleration, deceleration and speed reversal.

articleTitle: A Brushless Doubly Fed Machine for use in an Integrated Motor/Converter, Considering the Rotor Flux
publicationTitle: 2006 3rd IET International Conference on Power Electronics, Machines and Drives - PEMD 2006
abstract: The Brushless Doubly Fed Machine (BDFM) has received considerable attention recently, particularly in respect of analysis and performance as it has potential application where variable speed operation is required but limitations of cost and size demand a reduced-size converter. Any application of the BDFM in this way must accept a reduced speed range. A low rating use of such technology could be as an Integrated BDFM Motor/Converter where the application does not require a full speed range. This paper explores this application by assembling a prototype Integrated BDFM Motor/Converter from a commercial two-speed induction Motor, with modified rotor, and a commercial, first quadrant, PWM Converter. The design of the Motor affects the rating and operation of the Converter, in particular the balance between the stator winding MMFs, the design of the rotor slotting & winding to optimise the machine air gap flux. This paper investigates these issues on the prototype, using experimental test results & FE modelling to confirm the magnetic flux in the rotor.

articleTitle: Spectral Composition of Stator Vibrations Resulting from Modal Superposition in SRM
publicationTitle: 2006 3rd IET International Conference on Power Electronics, Machines and Drives - PEMD 2006
abstract: This paper presents a method to calculate the harmonic content of stator vibrations resulting from radial force excitations in switched reluctance machines (SRM). The method is based on a thin cylinder approximation of the stator. The dominant eigen modes are represented by their transmission impedance. The spectral composition of the vibrations can be calculated for each eigen mode using superposition of the vibrations caused by all phases of the SRM.

articleTitle: A Novel Prototype of Soft-Switching Inverter-Fed DC-DC Converter with Step-Up High-Frequency Planer Transformer Secondary-Side Phase-Shifted PWM Rectifier
publicationTitle: 2006 3rd IET International Conference on Power Electronics, Machines and Drives - PEMD 2006
abstract: This paper presents a novel circuit topology of isolated DC-DC power converter, which includes stable and efficient zero voltage soft switching (ZVS) full bridge inverter in the high frequency planer transformer primary-side and zero current soft switching rectifier in its secondary side. This power converter incorporates zero current soft switching (ZCS) phase-shifted PWM controlled two active power switches in series with either right or left leg of full-bridge rectifier in the transformer secondary-side. The proposed soft switching DC-DC power converter can achieve a wide soft-switching commutation under wide load variations from an extremely light load to a heavy load at a condition of constant frequency phase-shifted PWM voltage regulation and high conversion efficiency due to reduced circulating current and idling in the primary side of the transformer. The operating principle and the performance evaluations are discussed based on simulation analysis and experimental results obtained on a 2 kW rating and 40 kHz switching frequency breadboard power converter setup. The practical effectiveness of this soft-switching DC-DC power converter with a high frequency link is proven on the basis of simulation and experimental results.

articleTitle: Detecting Speed Fluctuations in D.C. Electric Motors Using a Radio Frequency Antenna Technique
publicationTitle: 2006 3rd IET International Conference on Power Electronics, Machines and Drives - PEMD 2006
abstract: This paper describes how the radio frequency (RF) signals generated during the mechanical commutation process in a D.C. electric motor can be used to estimate the motors rotational speed and also any oscillations in the motor speed. Amplitude and frequency modulated signals were added to the voltage supply of a D.C. electric motor to simulate fault conditions in the system. The R.F. signals generated during the commutation process were captured using a antenna which was interfaced to a high speed PCI interface card. The captured data was then processed using MATLAB. The results presented show the spectrums produced for a motor running at constant rotational speed and also with sinusoidal oscillations or fluctuations added to the motor rotational speed. Peaks in the spectrums are correlated to the motor speed and oscillations in the motor speed.

articleTitle: Single-Phase Active Rectifier Selection for Fault Tolerant Machine
publicationTitle: 2006 3rd IET International Conference on Power Electronics, Machines and Drives - PEMD 2006
abstract: A fault tolerant, 5-phase PM generator has been developed for use on the low pressure (LP) shaft of an aircraft gas turbine engine. The machine operates at variable speed and therefore has a variable voltage, variable frequency electrical output (VVVF). The generator is to be used to provide a 350V DC bus for distribution throughout the aircraft, and a study has been carried out that identifies the most suitable AC-DC converter topology for this machine in terms of losses, electrical component ratings, filtering requirements and circuit complexity.

articleTitle: Wavelet Based Diagnosis and Protection of Three-Phase Induction Motor Fed from Sinusoidal PWM Voltage Source Inverter
publicationTitle: 2006 3rd IET International Conference on Power Electronics, Machines and Drives - PEMD 2006
abstract: In this work, a novel wavelet packet transform based algorithm is developed for the on-line protection of three-phase induction motor fed from a sinusoidal pulse width modulated voltage source inverter (PWM-VSI). The algorithm is implemented in real-time using the DS1102 digital signal processor board. The criterion for the protection is the comparison of wavelet packet transform (WPT) coefficients of the second level high frequency sub-band of three-phase line currents using the selected mother wavelet `db3' with a threshold determined experimentally during the healthy condition of the motor. The minimum description length and the Shannon entropy criteria are used for selecting the optimal mother wavelet and optimal number of levels of resolution, respectively. In all the tests carried out, the proposed algorithm identified the disturbances properly and initiated the trip signal almost at the instant or within one cycle of the fault occurrence.

articleTitle: Generated Voltage Harmonics Minimization of Radial Permanent Magnet Single-Phase AC Linear Generator
publicationTitle: 2006 3rd IET International Conference on Power Electronics, Machines and Drives - PEMD 2006
abstract: Two-dimensional finite element method is used in the analysis to calculate the magnetic field parameters in a radial permanent magnet linear single-phase AC generator. Both surface and internal permanent magnet schemes are analyzed and compared according to three different parameters; the cogging force, the induced AC voltage and the THD of the induced AC voltage. Three different design structures were used to reduce the THD of the induced voltage; tooth shoe, stepped tooth and chamfered tooth. The chamfered tooth provides as low THD as 4% and 12% for surface and internal prototype schemes, respectively. The cogging force was much reduced using the stator optimal length; for both schemes, in addition to the total generator weight is reduced.

articleTitle: A Single-Phase Hybrid Active Power Filter Connected to a Photovoltaic Array
publicationTitle: 2006 3rd IET International Conference on Power Electronics, Machines and Drives - PEMD 2006
abstract: Due to the proliferation of nonlinear and switching loads from power electronics converters, there is an increasing concern to control and reduce the harmonic currents in distribution power lines. These types of loads draw nonsinusoidal currents from the mains, causing harmonic distortion. One of the methods to reduce the problem is by using the power electronics approach. This paper presents a single-phase hybrid active power filter connected to a photovoltaic array. The uniqueness of the proposed scheme is the fact that it improves the filtering performance of the conventional shunt active power filter, as well as simultaneously supplies the power from the photovoltaic array to the load. The compensation current reference estimation is based on the extension instantaneous reactive-power theorem. Experimental results obtained from a laboratory system that verifies the viability and effectiveness of the proposed scheme are presented.

articleTitle: Direct Torque Control of PM Brushless AC Motors Having Non-sinusoidal Back-emf Waveforms
publicationTitle: 2006 3rd IET International Conference on Power Electronics, Machines and Drives - PEMD 2006
abstract: This paper describes the application of direct torque control (DTC) to a PM brushless AC machine whose back-emf waveform is non-sinusoidal, and compares its performance with that which is achieved when the back-emf waveform is assumed to be sinusoidal. It also demonstrates the utility of employing a sliding mode observer to estimate the back-emf waveform, and, thereby, to calculate the instantaneous electromagnetic torque and to minimise torque ripple. The effectiveness of this approach is validated by both simulations and measurements.

articleTitle: A Novel Current Injection Based Twelve-Pulse Rectifier that Applies Single Three-Phase Diode Bridge
publicationTitle: 2006 3rd IET International Conference on Power Electronics, Machines and Drives - PEMD 2006
abstract: A novel twelve-pulse rectifier that applies single three-phase diode bridge and current injection technique is presented. The rectifier applies a lossless current injection network and a passive voltage loaded resistance emulator. Optimization of the resistance emulator transformer turns ratio is performed, and resulting waveforms of the rectifier input current and output voltage are the same as in conventional twelve-pulse rectifiers. The input current THD is reduced to 15.22%. The results are experimentally verified on a 2 kW rectifier.

articleTitle: Approaches to Network Protection for Inverter Dominated Electrical Distribution Systems
publicationTitle: 2006 3rd IET International Conference on Power Electronics, Machines and Drives - PEMD 2006
abstract: The use of the micro-grid paradigm with extensive inverter interfaced generation raises the problem of severely restricted fault levels when operating in a power island. This paper presents a review of the conventional distribution network protection practices and then discusses their limitations when applied to inverter dominated micro-grids. The use of voltage measurement based fault detection is considered and is followed by consideration of how to apply this technique in conjunction with an adaptive form of protection. A potential solution for small micro-grids is presented in the form of voltage controlled overcurrent devices to enable the use of lower current threshold settings. Key issues for the design of network protection within micro-grids are summarised.

articleTitle: Analysis of Power Quality in a DC Tram System
publicationTitle: 2006 3rd IET International Conference on Power Electronics, Machines and Drives - PEMD 2006
abstract: This paper describes the development of a model for electrified transit systems. The model is developed for the analysis of power quality in a DC tram system. This paper presents a new, more computationally efficient modular approach to modelling electrified transit systems. The technique applied separates the train movement analysis from the electrical network analysis and uses differential equations to simulate the train movement and nodal voltage analysis to evaluate the electrical network.

articleTitle: Sensitivity of active front-end ASDs and DFIGs to voltage sags and short interruptions
publicationTitle: 2006 3rd IET International Conference on Power Electronics, Machines and Drives - PEMD 2006
abstract: Detailed modelling and performance assessment of a three-phase active front-end driven ASD was conducted in PSCAD/ EMTDC. Studies were developed to identify and evaluate the dynamic performance characteristics of the ASD and a sensitivity assessment to various voltage disturbances was carried out. The ASD is controlled using typical closed loop V-Hz and also closed-loop vector control. A voltage sag generator was used to conduct simulations and sensitivity assessments of ASD and other power electronic applications such as variable-speed wind turbines based on Doubly Fed Induction Generators (DFIGs). The ASD and DFIG sensitivity performance was assessed in the event of three-phase, two-phase and single-phase voltage sags for typical speed and torque operating conditions. Voltage tolerance curves were also obtained and analysed for both active front-end ASD and DFIG with different types of voltage sags and torque-speed operating conditions.

articleTitle: Simulation of Linear Induction Generators in Hybrid Electric Vehicle Applications
publicationTitle: 2006 3rd IET International Conference on Power Electronics, Machines and Drives - PEMD 2006
abstract: Using linear induction machines in hybrid electric vehicles has some advantages such as robustness, reliability over convectional generators that is used in this system. This paper suggests a three phase self excited linear induction generator (SELIG) for a system of free-piston generator. Linear induction machine has some configurations. A flat ladder type linear induction is used as generator in simulations. Design of the machine is carried and finite element method is used to simulate the performance of generator.

articleTitle: Rating Requirements of a Unified Power Quality Conditioner (UPQC) for Voltage Ride Through Capability Enhancement
publicationTitle: 2006 3rd IET International Conference on Power Electronics, Machines and Drives - PEMD 2006
abstract: The problem of voltage ride through capability of fixed speed wind generation as a result of voltage sags is examined by means of a simulation study. The role of a Unified Power Quality Conditioner (UPQC), which provides both shunt and series compensation, in enhancing the ride through capability is investigated under both full and partial voltage restoration. Results of a study to identify the minimum rating requirements to ensure stability are presented.

articleTitle: Estimation of the Induction Machine Behaviour Subjected to Voltage Sags
publicationTitle: 2006 3rd IET International Conference on Power Electronics, Machines and Drives - PEMD 2006
abstract: The voltage sags is probably one of the most important problems of the power quality that affects the performance of ac induction motors. Hence, this paper will focus on that by taking into account the different voltage sags types, considering variations in the phase angle and variations of the mechanical load of the motor. The behaviour of the induction motor under such conditions is analyzed. The simulations were carried out by means of a simplified induction motor model on Matlab.

articleTitle: Structurally Integrated Slotless PM Brushless Motor with Spiral Wound Laminations for Marine Thrusters
publicationTitle: 2006 3rd IET International Conference on Power Electronics, Machines and Drives - PEMD 2006
abstract: Rim driven thrusters with structurally integrated brushless PM motors are now an established technology with an increasing range of applications. In these thrusters, the stator of the motor is housed within the thruster duct, and the rotor forms a ring around the tips of the propeller. Such high pole number motors tend to be very thin radialy, have very small length to diameter ratios, and have relatively large airgaps to accommodate corrosion protection layers on the surfaces of the rotor and stator. The relatively large diameter stator laminations of such machines tend therefore to have very thin back of core and narrow teeth, which make them expensive and difficult to manufacture. This paper proposes an alternative potentially lower cost motor topology featuring a slotless stator whose laminations are manufactured from a single strip of steel that is edge wound into a spiral (like a "slinky" and then fitted over the windings that are preformed on the outside surface of a non-conducting former. The former is also part of the sealed housing that protects the stator from corrosion in seawater. The paper discusses the design optimisation of such a motor using analytical and finite element analysis (FEA), describes a demonstrator motor and reports experimental and FEA results.

articleTitle: Single-Phase Switched Reluctance Drive with Saturation-Based Starting Method
publicationTitle: 2006 3rd IET International Conference on Power Electronics, Machines and Drives - PEMD 2006
abstract: This paper presents a low cost switched reluctance drive with single-phase configuration. Generally, the single-phase switched reluctance machine (SRM) cannot produce a continuous positive torque over one revolution. Hence the machine cannot start from every rotor position. This problem is solved with a saturation-based starting method. The basic principles of this method, experimental results, as well as a new strategy for a fast start up are introduced.

articleTitle: Power and Energy Management Policy Implementation of a Dual-Energy Source Electric Vehicle
publicationTitle: 2006 3rd IET International Conference on Power Electronics, Machines and Drives - PEMD 2006
abstract: This paper reports progressive work in implementing a power and energy management policy for an Electric Vehicle (EV) sourced by batteries and ultracapacitors. The sequential decision process of determining the power split ratio and reference energy levels of the dual sources has been concisely represented as a state transition mechanism. Experimental results from our test vehicle were used to validate simulation models of tractive power demands and battery behaviour. The overall approach is design oriented, with the objective of contributing towards completeness of the EV power and energy management problem description.

articleTitle: Dynamic Modelling of a High-Speed Single-Phase PM Brushless DC Drive
publicationTitle: 2006 3rd IET International Conference on Power Electronics, Machines and Drives - PEMD 2006
abstract: The dynamic simulation of a 45krpm, 1kW, single-phase brushless dc motor, when it is supplied from a full-bridge inverter and a half-bridge inverter, is described. The electromagnetic performance is modelled, with due account of the stator iron loss, rotor eddy current loss and the friction loss, and simulated results are validated experimentally.

articleTitle: Performance Improvement using Simple PID Controller Tuning Formulae
publicationTitle: 2006 3rd IET International Conference on Power Electronics, Machines and Drives - PEMD 2006
abstract: The proportional integral derivative (PID) controller is the most dominant form of automatic controller in industrial use today. With this technique, it is necessary to adjust the controller parameters according to the nature of the process. Thus, for effective control of a HVDC system, for example, specific values need to be chosen for the P, I and D parameters, which will be different for the values required to control, for example, an induction motor drive. This tailoring of controller to process is known as controller tuning. Controller tuning is easily and effectively performed using tuning rules (i.e. formulae for controller tuning, based on process information). Such tuning rules allow the easy set up of controllers to achieve optimum performance at commissioning. Importantly, they allow ease of re-commissioning if the characteristics of the process change. The paper communicates the results of recent work in the collation of industry-relevant PI and PID controller tuning rules, which may be applied to a variety of applications in power electronics, machines and drives.

articleTitle: Cogging Force Minimization of Linear Engine-Coupled Tubular Permanent Magnet Linear AC Synchronous Generator
publicationTitle: 2006 3rd IET International Conference on Power Electronics, Machines and Drives - PEMD 2006
abstract: Various methods have been discussed to reduce the cogging force in tubular permanent magnet type linear single phase AC generator. In particular, the proposed methods of cogging force reduction depend on the variations of the permanent magnet construction. These methods include two approaches in the form of sloped magnets, and conical magnets in addition to the conventional method of varying the magnet length. The undesired cogging force ripples are calculated by a two dimensional Finite Element Method. Moreover, the generated electromotive force in the stator coils is calculated for each configuration of the permanent magnet. The experimental results agreed well with those obtained from the FEM-based simulations.

articleTitle: Piezoelectric Actuators for Active Vibration Damping of Switched Reluctance Motors
publicationTitle: 2006 3rd IET International Conference on Power Electronics, Machines and Drives - PEMD 2006
abstract: This paper presents an active vibration control using piezoelectric actuators for switched reluctance motors. An experimental single-phase structure with no rotor is used in order to confirm Finite-Element results showing the efficiency of the piezoelectric elements for this application. Location and design of these actuators are discussed. The experimental results are first given for sinusoidal excitations, and then a Positive Position Feedback controller is studied for the closed loop control, which is necessary in classical use of the motor.

articleTitle: Concentrated Wound 45 kW, 420 rpm Permanent Magnet Machine with Embedded Magnets
publicationTitle: 2006 3rd IET International Conference on Power Electronics, Machines and Drives - PEMD 2006
abstract: A 45 kW prototype machine with 12-slot-10-pole, q = 0.4 structure was constructed in order to obtain practical experiences of concentrated wound PM-machines. The measurement results provide essential information to verify the analytical calculations and also the results obtained with 2D FEA. The winding type studied consists of concentrated pole windings. The number of slots per pole and phase q < 0.5. Concentrated wound motors create harmonics and sub-harmonics, which may cause extra heating, additional losses and vibration. Therefore, the importance of manufacturing a prototype machine of considerable power e.g. 45 kW should be stressed. It was in the authors' interest to verify if the harmonics have a great impact on the losses.

articleTitle: The Variable-Capacitance Machine for Off-shore Wind Generation
publicationTitle: 2006 3rd IET International Conference on Power Electronics, Machines and Drives - PEMD 2006
abstract: The paper presents a feasibility study that considers Variable-Capacitance (V-C) machines to be contenders for the direct generation of High Voltage Direct Current (HVDC) power in offshore wind farm applications. The study uses 3D finite element analysis to predict the generator capacitance variation with rotor position and a Matlab / Simulink model to predict the machine operation and circuit optimisation. A small prototype machine has been built and tested to provide some validation of the simulation studies.

articleTitle: Fault Level due to Interconnection of Embedded Generator
publicationTitle: 2006 3rd IET International Conference on Power Electronics, Machines and Drives - PEMD 2006
abstract: Embedded generator (EG) is simply a small-scale generating unit (up to 20 MW) whose total output will be consumed by loads at the medium voltage (MV) distribution levels. One of the technical challenges faced is the fault level management, as connection of EG results in increased fault level beyond the capacity of switchgear and cable. This paper presents a fault level analysis and stability of an EG connected to a generic distribution network. With the model of four different types of networks, i.e. interconnected network without EG, interconnected network with EG, use of reactor with EG and network splitting with EG network, developed in PSSIViper, simulations were performed to determine the suitability of network splitting for effective fault level reduction and also to determine the behavioural characteristics of the EG with respect to transient stability when faults were initiated. The studies show that the network splitting method is most suitable for reducing the fault level.

articleTitle: Mechanical Design Tools for Low Speed High Torque Electrical Machines
publicationTitle: 2006 3rd IET International Conference on Power Electronics, Machines and Drives - PEMD 2006
abstract: To minimise overall mass the designer needs mechanical design tools to link the machine structure to airgap deflection. A polynomial modelling technique applied to finite element results for radial-flux structures is introduced and used on a real example. The relationship between airgap clearance and flux density is explored for both axial-and radial-flux machines. Typical adjustments to these basic equations are found.

articleTitle: Modelling Axial Variations in Induction Motors with Rotor Skew using Multi-sliced 2D Finite Element Analysis
publicationTitle: 2006 3rd IET International Conference on Power Electronics, Machines and Drives - PEMD 2006
abstract: This paper reports on a finite element study (using Flux 2D) carried out on a cage induction motor and uses an axial multi-sliced model to incorporate rotor skew. This model includes inter-bar current and assesses the effect of this on the starting torque. An analytical simulation (in PC-IMD) is also used to investigate the performance in terms of the torque-speed curves and the results are compared to a set of experimental results from a number of nominally identical machines.

articleTitle: A Novel Switched Capacitor Lossless Inductors Quasi-Resonant Snubber Assisted ZCS PWM High Frequency Series Load Resonant Inverter
publicationTitle: 2006 3rd IET International Conference on Power Electronics, Machines and Drives - PEMD 2006
abstract: In this paper, a novel type of auxiliary switched capacitor assisted edge resonant soft-switching ZCS PWM quasi-resonant lossless inductor is proposed for consumer induction heating appliances. The operation principle of this high frequency inverter is described using the switching mode equivalent circuits. This newly developed multi resonant high frequency inverter can regulate its high frequency output AC power under a principle of constant frequency edge-resonant zero current soft switching commutation by asymmetrical PWM control scheme. The high frequency power regulation and actual power conversion efficiency characteristics of consumer IH products using the proposed ZCS PWM series load resonant high frequency inverter are evaluated. The practical effectiveness and operating performances of ZCS PWM high frequency inverter are discussed on the basis of simulation and experimental results as compared with the conventional soft switching high frequency inverters.

articleTitle: Stability of a MicroGrid
publicationTitle: 2006 3rd IET International Conference on Power Electronics, Machines and Drives - PEMD 2006
abstract: The demand for electricity continues to grow globally and the fonnation of MicroGrids is becoming a potentially attractive option to meet the expanding energy demands. A MicroGrid consists of a cluster of micro sources, energy storage systems (e.g. flywheel) and loads, operating as a single controllable system. A MicroGrid can be operated both connected to the main grid or as an island and must maintain its stability during both these modes of operation. This paper therefore investigates the important area of stability of a MicroGrid. An in-depth simulation study on stable operation of MicroGrids during faults is demonstrated and discussed in this paper with supporting PSCAD/ EMTDC results.

articleTitle: Improved Sensorless Operation of Interior PM Brushless AC Motor Drive with Reduced-Order EKF
publicationTitle: 2006 3rd IET International Conference on Power Electronics, Machines and Drives - PEMD 2006
abstract: It is a challenge to realise an EKF-based sensorless controller for an interior permanent magnet (IPM) brushless ac motor drive due to the influence of non-linearity and rotor saliency. An improved reduced-order EKF method is presented which reduces the rotor position estimation error of an IPM motor, which was evident in [1] due to the neglect of saliency. The effectiveness of the proposed method is verified experimentally.

articleTitle: Manufacturing Methods of Stator Cores with Concentrated Windings
publicationTitle: 2006 3rd IET International Conference on Power Electronics, Machines and Drives - PEMD 2006
abstract: The purpose of this paper is to investigate the difficulties in manufacturing a stator core with concentrated windings. The existing solutions are compared in terms of cost, required equipment for the production and performance of the permanent-magnet (PM) motor. A 1 kW 28-pole PM motor with an outer diameter of 400mm, designed for a low-speed direct-driven application is taken as an example.

articleTitle: The Effect of the Number of Rotor Slits on the Performance Characteristics of Medium-Speed Solid Rotor Induction Motor
publicationTitle: 2006 3rd IET International Conference on Power Electronics, Machines and Drives - PEMD 2006
abstract: The effect of the number of rotor slits on the electromagnetic torque production, torque ripple, rotor eddy-current loss and the power factor are numerically studied in case of a three phase, two-pole, 200 Hz, solid-rotor induction motor. The number of the stator slots was 48 and the number of the rotor slits was varied from 28 to 36. The depth of the rotor slits was kept at a constant value in all the calculations. The harmonic content of the air-gap flux density as well as the electro-magnetic torque at each rotor slit number were studied in detail. It was also found that when the number of the rotor slits was an odd number, an unsymmetrical magnetic pull affects between the stator and the rotor.

articleTitle: Spike Suppression in a Bidirectional High-Frequency Transformer-Link Inverter Using a Regenerative Snubber
publicationTitle: 2006 3rd IET International Conference on Power Electronics, Machines and Drives - PEMD 2006
abstract: This paper presents a spike suppression method for Bidirectional High-Frequency Link (BHFL) inverter using a regenerative snubber.
